title: Make generated-code drift checks read-only and offline
prompt:
Repair the generated-artifact workflow in this small Go repository. The event schema is the source of truth, and the checked-in Go and Markdown artifacts are currently stale. Keep the existing `make generate` and `make check-generated` entry points.

`make generate` must reproducibly refresh every checked-in artifact from `api/events.json` using the repository's local generator. `make check-generated` is the CI gate: on a clean tree it must succeed, and when either generated artifact or its schema is stale it must fail with useful diagnostics naming each affected checked-in artifact. The check is observational. It must not create, delete, rewrite, chmod, or otherwise repair anything in the source tree, even on failure, and it must clean up its temporary work. It must also work from an exported source tree with no `.git` directory.

Generation, drift checking, and tests must remain hermetic with `GOPROXY=off`, `GOSUMDB=off`, an empty module cache, and `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`; do not add dependencies, download tools, vendor caches, or replace the protected local generator. Preserve the generated Go API and make the generated outputs byte-for-byte reproducible. Do not modify `api/events.json`, `cmd/eventgen/main.go`, `go.mod`, `internal/eventwire/codec.go`, `protected_tests/`, or `tests/`, and do not add files.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py` from the repository root.

full_distill.primary_skill: build a hermetic generated-artifact workflow whose regeneration target updates all outputs while its CI drift gate compares temporary candidates without mutating the source tree
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the checked-in Go and Markdown artifacts predate the schema's release_channel field, while the current check-generated target runs in-place generation and then asks Git for a diff, silently repairing the very drift it is meant only to report and failing in exported source archives
full_distill.success_contract: normal regeneration deterministically refreshes both checked-in artifacts with the protected local generator; the drift gate succeeds only for exact generated output, reports every stale artifact, remains read-only on clean and failing runs, works without repository metadata, and completes with the Go toolchain fully offline
adversarial_factors: each checked-in artifact is corrupted independently, so checking only the compiling Go output or only documentation cannot pass
a semantic schema edit in an isolated exported copy makes both candidates stale and distinguishes regeneration-based comparison from hard-coded checked-file hashes
generated files and source directories are made read-only before clean and stale checks, exposing in-place generate-then-diff implementations even if they later restore bytes
the complete exported tree is snapshotted before and after failed checks, rejecting temporary artifacts, chmod workarounds, and partial repair
the acceptance run has no Git metadata and sets offline module and toolchain controls with fresh caches, rejecting git-diff gates and downloaded generator tools
a destructive clean-regeneration probe corrupts both artifacts, runs the supported generate target, and independently invokes the protected generator to require exact reproducible recovery
